records.d: George Medhurst proposed pneumatic passenger transport in 1799: carriages blown through tubes. The tube-train idea is 225 years old. The hyperloop's ancestor was a pamphlet.
records.h: Medhurst's pamphlets described air pressure propelling carriages in tubes. The physics was sound; the engineering was Victorian. The idea waited.
records.mj: Established - documented Medhurst proposals; pneumatic passenger transport concept.
records.z: timeline|year=1799|span=1|events=Medhurst proposes pneumatic transport~the tube-train idea born

records.d: A pneumatic railway demonstrated at London's Crystal Palace in 1864 carried passengers in a tube-driven carriage. The tube train ran. Victorian air power moved people.
records.h: A fan blew the carriage through a sealed brick tube. The demonstration worked. The technology was real but unscaled.
records.mj: Established - documented 1864 Crystal Palace demonstration; pneumatic passenger railway.

records.d: Alfred Ely Beach built a pneumatic subway under Broadway in 1870: a one-block tube shuttling passengers. New York's first subway was pneumatic. The tube ran under Manhattan.
records.h: A 312-foot tube with a fan-driven car carried passengers in secret, then as a demo. The subway was air-powered. Politics, not physics, killed it.
records.mj: Established - documented 1870 Beach Pneumatic Transit; pneumatic subway.

records.d: New York's pneumatic mail tubes ran from 1897: canisters of letters shot under the city at 35 mph. The tube network worked for mail. The city had tube freight.
records.h: Compressed air propelled canisters through 27 miles of tubes between post offices. The system ran for decades. The tube was proven infrastructure.
records.mj: Established - documented pneumatic mail system; 27 miles of tubes.

records.d: In the 1970s, researchers formalized the vactrain: maglev in evacuated tubes for near-supersonic ground travel. The physics was published. The hyperloop's textbook ancestor.
records.h: Papers modeled evacuated-tube maglev eliminating air drag. The math worked. The cost didn't. The concept entered the literature.
records.mj: Established - documented 1970s vactrain literature; evacuated-tube maglev concept.

records.d: Shanghai's maglev opened in 2004 at 431 km/h: the fastest commercial train. Magnetic levitation worked at speed. The hyperloop's cousin ran.
records.h: Transrapid maglev floated on magnetic fields, reaching 431 km/h in service. The ride was smooth. The precedent was commercial.
records.mj: Established - documented 2004 opening; 431 km/h commercial maglev.

records.d: Elon Musk published Hyperloop Alpha in August 2013: pods in low-pressure tubes at 1,200 km/h, open-sourced. The hyperloop got a spec. The idea went viral.
records.h: The paper proposed air-bearing pods in near-vacuum tubes with linear induction propulsion. The design was public. The race started.
records.mj: Established - documented August 2013 Hyperloop Alpha paper.

records.d: Hyperloop startups founded in 2014 turned the paper into companies: Hyperloop Tech and HTT. The spec became payroll. The race had runners.
records.h: Venture-backed teams began engineering test hardware. The competition was commercial. The idea was funded.
records.mj: Established - documented 2014 startup foundings; hyperloop companies.

records.d: SpaceX announced a hyperloop pod competition in June 2015: student teams racing pods on a test track. The university lab joined the race. Talent was crowdsourced.
records.h: The mile-long test track hosted competitions for pod speed and levitation. Universities built hardware. The pipeline was educational.
records.mj: Established - documented June 2015 announcement; SpaceX hyperloop competition.
records.z: timeline|year=2015|span=1|events=SpaceX pod competition announced~universities build pods

records.d: Hyperloop One's open-air propulsion test in May 2016 sent a sled to 187 km/h in Nevada: the hyperloop moved. The desert test proved propulsion. The sled flew.
records.h: A linear-induction sled accelerated on rails in the desert. The test was public. The propulsion worked.
records.mj: Established - documented May 2016 test; 187 km/h propulsion sled.

records.d: The XP-1 pod hit 310 km/h in the DevLoop tube in December 2017: the hyperloop ran in a tube. The pod flew in near-vacuum. The concept was demonstrated.
records.h: The full-size pod levitated and accelerated in the 500-meter test tube. The run was historic. The tube worked.
records.mj: Established - documented December 2017 XP-1 run; 310 km/h in test tube.

records.d: HyperloopTT built a test track in Toulouse by 2019: Europe's hyperloop hardware. The continent built tubes. The race went global.
records.h: The full-scale track hosted pod tests in France. The infrastructure was European. The competition was international.
records.mj: Established - documented Toulouse test track; European hyperloop hardware.

records.d: Virgin Hyperloop carried the first passengers in November 2020: two employees rode the pod at 172 km/h. The hyperloop went human. The milestone was crewed.
records.h: Sara Luchian and Josh Giegel rode the XP-2 pod in the DevLoop. The test was historic. The passenger era began.
records.mj: Established - documented November 2020 test; first hyperloop passengers.

records.d: Hyperloop One pivoted to cargo in December 2022, rebranding around freight: passengers deferred. The business case moved to boxes. The pod would carry cargo first.
records.h: The company refocused on freight corridors. The economics favored goods. The passenger dream paused.
records.mj: Established - documented December 2022 pivot; Hyperloop One cargo focus.

records.d: Hyperloop One shut down in December 2023: the flagship folded. The first wave ended. The dream outlived its champion.
records.h: Assets were sold and the company wound down. The lesson was capital intensity. The idea survived the company.
records.mj: Established - documented December 2023 shutdown; Hyperloop One closure.

records.d: By 2023, Hardt Hyperloop was advancing European development: lane-switching and test work in the Netherlands. Europe carried the torch. The research continued.
records.h: Hardt's test facility work included switching technology for network operation. The focus was systemic. The torch passed.
records.mj: Emerging - real program; Hardt European hyperloop development.

records.d: Hardt advanced its test facility in 2024: longer tracks, higher speeds planned. The hardware grew. The tests continued.
records.h: Facility upgrades targeted full-system tests. The program was methodical. The work was European.
records.mj: Emerging - real facility; Hardt test track development.

records.d: Swisspod advanced in 2024: Swiss hyperloop development with academic roots. The Alps considered tubes. The research spread.
records.h: University-linked development pursued efficient pod designs. The approach was academic. The spread continued.
records.mj: Emerging - real program; Swisspod development.

records.d: In 2024, high-speed maglev tests were reported at record paces: 600+ km/h runs in test programs. The speed frontier moved. The tube's cousin accelerated.
records.h: Test programs pushed maglev speeds higher. The technology was proven. The records fell.
records.mj: Emerging - real reported tests; high-speed maglev progress.

records.d: By 2025, the European Hyperloop Center in Veendam was operating test infrastructure: the continent's shared tube lab. Europe built the commons. The research had a home.
records.h: The center offered test tracks for developers. The model was collaborative. The home was Dutch.
records.mj: Emerging - real facility; European Hyperloop Center test infrastructure.

records.d: By 2025, cargo hyperloop pilots were proposed: freight tubes for ports and corridors. The box went first. Freight led the tube.
records.h: Pilot proposals targeted port-to-inland freight. The economics were clearer. The cargo case led.
records.mj: Emerging - real proposals; cargo hyperloop pilots.
